edits.text: 1. PRIVILEGE OBJECTION. Defendant objects to production of material protected by the attorney-client privilege, work-product doctrine, or other applicable protection. Each objection will be stated specifically in the response to the particular request, identifying the protection asserted and its basis, stating whether responsive material is being withheld, and describing the scope of that withholding without revealing protected information.
edits.name: Request-specific privilege objections

edits.text: 2. PRODUCTION. Within 14 days after the parties agree to these production terms, Defendant will serve request-specific responses and begin rolling production of responsive, nonprivileged materials. Each response will state any objection and its specific grounds, whether responsive materials are being withheld on those grounds, the scope of any withholding, and the scope and timing of production. Defendant will complete production within 30 days after agreement. These terms do not extend or supersede any existing deadline absent express agreement or court order. Plaintiff reserves all existing deadlines and rights to seek relief.
edits.name: Responses, rolling production, and reservation of rights

edits.text: 3. PRIVILEGE LOG. Defendant will provide a privilege log contemporaneously with each rolling production identifying responsive materials withheld on privilege or protection grounds during the corresponding review. The log will identify each withheld item and provide its date, document type, author or sender, recipients and their roles where relevant, a description of its subject matter sufficient to assess the claim without revealing protected information, and the specific privilege or protection asserted and its basis. Defendant will complete the log no later than the production-completion deadline. Any categorical treatment or exclusion from logging requires agreement of the parties or court order.
edits.name: Contemporaneous privilege log
